 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Lisandro Martinez has been blasted as "unacceptable" after the Manchester United defender conceded a penalty and got sent off for hitting out at Wesley Fofana.
 Michael Carrick's side were the better team in the first half and would have been 1-0 up at half time had Matheus Cunha not strayed into a marginally offside position before finding the net. In the second half, Martinez was at fault for Chelsea's first goal, as Morgan Rogers got past him too easily before scooping a fine finish over Senne Lammens.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, a few moments later, the Argentine struck Wesley Fofana in the face in the box, conceding a penalty and earning himself a second yellow card. After he was dismissed, TNT Sport commentator Ally McCoist tore into the Argentine.

 Man United manager had no tactical prowess so I left for Chelsea - he was very upset with me

 After a Chelsea corner was swung to the back post, Martinez had his back to the corner when he hit Fofana in the face with both hands. The referee did not see the incident, but VAR intervened, leading to Martinez's red card.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement When the replay came up, McCoist said: "Ridiculous defending, you're just jumping into him, that's a penalty. Somebody explain to me why that's not a penalty?"
 Not long after the decision was made, McCoist added: "It's unacceptable, absolutely unacceptable. He runs right across, look, absolutely crazy, crazy."
 Martinez's red card ended any hope of a comeback at Stamford Bridge -Credit:2026 Catherine Ivill - AMA
 McCoist then added: "Exactly who I'm thinking about right now, Michael Carrick. Look at that. He can't look at him and nor should he. He's not looked at him and nor should he."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Only one minute and 22 seconds separated Martinez's first and second yellow cards. His implosion all but ended United's hopes of getting back at Stamford Bridge.
 Carrick's feelings on the Argentine could be inferred by the fact he did not even acknowledge him when he trudged down the tunnel.
